transformation_B_totals.note: These totals are counted AFTER Transformation A already invalidated the anomaly row's dishwasher1 (-125.236) and refrigerator1 (-779.25) cells, so those two values are correctly excluded here (they were converted to NaN/invalid by Transformation A, not to zero by Transformation B). A later independent recount directly on the pre-transformation aligned file (see verification_v2_independent_corrected.negative_conversion_totals_independent) counts negative values in the INPUT file before either transformation, which includes those 2 anomaly cells -- giving dishwasher1=79731 and refrigerator1=346 there. The two totals differ by exactly 1 per affected appliance, fully explained by this ordering difference; both are internally consistent.

verification_v1_original_flawed_check.note: Retained for audit trail. This check used an incorrect, overly broad criterion -- see verification_correction_notes below.

verification_correction_notes.problem_with_original_check: The original check counted ALL rows in the OUTPUT file where both dishwasher1 and refrigerator1 are simultaneously null and invalid, expecting exactly 1. This is the wrong test: the dataset already contained 2,400 rows with this exact pattern BEFORE Stage 5 ran, because Stage 4's reindexing legitimately marked both dishwasher1 and refrigerator1 missing at the same timestamps in several homes (both submeters happened to be missing together). An absolute whole-file count of 2,401 cannot distinguish '2,400 pre-existing + 1 new' from any other combination -- it just looked like a failure against a naive expectation of exactly 1.
verification_correction_notes.cross_check_against_stage4_report: These counts match Stage 4's own appliance_invalid_counts exactly for dishwasher1 and refrigerator1 in these four home/split combinations (both appliances had identical invalid counts in each case, confirming both submeters shared the same missing-minute pattern). 8386 is absent from this list because its dishwasher1/refrigerator1 invalid counts were 0 in Stage 4 (its missingness was in air1 instead).
verification_correction_notes.corrected_methodology: Instead of an absolute count, merge the pre-transformation (aligned) and post-transformation (modeling) files on (dataid, split, utc_dt), then count rows where dishwasher1_valid and refrigerator1_valid BOTH flip from True (in aligned) to False (in modeling). This isolates exactly what Stage 5 changed, independent of any pre-existing missingness pattern.
verification_correction_notes.corrected_result: Exactly 1 row flips from valid to invalid for both fields: dataid=7901, split=train, utc_dt=2018-09-22 01:54:00 -- precisely the intended anomaly row and no other. post_both_invalid_total (2401) minus pre_existing_both_invalid_total (2400) = 1, confirming no other row was affected.

verification_v2_independent_corrected.method: Full merge of aligned (input) and modeling (output) files on (dataid, split, utc_dt); row-count and column-list checks; per-column identity checks on dataid/split/utc_dt/local_dt using NaT-safe pandas .equals(); explicit valid-to-invalid and invalid-to-valid flip counts for all three appliances; full value-level aggregate comparison (not just negative-count comparison); independent recount of negative-to-zero conversions directly from the files; file stat (size/mtime) checks on the two preserved upstream files.

negative_conversion_totals_independent.note: Counted directly from the pre-transformation aligned file; includes the 2 anomaly cells (differs from transformation_B_totals by exactly 1 per affected appliance -- see note there).
